task_instance: Build a minimal Cloudflare Worker app on the stable @cloudflare/sandbox package that exposes a /run?cmd=... endpoint which executes a shell command inside an isolated per-user sandbox via sandbox.exec() and returns buffered stdout/stderr/exitCode, following the skill's Section 1 gate check (confirm package/image are stable, not @next) and Section 2 contract (exec resolves with buffered output).
blocker_detail: The skill's core deliverable is a working, deployed Cloudflare Sandbox app, not just source text. Producing that requires: (1) running `npm install` and `tsc`/typecheck against the installed stable @cloudflare/sandbox types (the skill explicitly says 'trust installed stable types' over guesses -- there is no way to install or inspect real types without running npm), (2) running `wrangler dev`/`wrangler deploy` to actually build the container image and Durable Object binding and confirm the Worker boots, and (3) invoking the deployed /run endpoint to confirm sandbox.exec() really returns buffered stdout/stderr/exitCode from a live container. All of this requires executing code/CLI commands, which this runtime cannot do (no Bash/code execution, no package installation), and real deployment additionally requires a Cloudflare account/credentials, which the safety rules forbid using. I could only author the source files and check them by eye against the API shape returned by a web search of the public docs (WebFetch to developers.cloudflare.com was itself blocked by the egress proxy), so the deliverable was never actually run or verified to work -- only its text was produced.
